name: North River steamboat passenger service
description: The North River Steamboat carried passengers between New York and Albany on the Hudson. Robert Fulton identified its engine as the one Boulton & Watt made for him in 1804.

impact.note: First lasting commercial steamboat service, reorganising river travel in one region; river and coastal steam navigation grew from it.

places.note: Place refers to the sourced event; historic political boundaries are not inferred.

date.basis: Date stated in the cited source.

events.statement: A September advertisement offered a scheduled North River steamboat passage to Albany for seven dollars.

evidence.locator: 2 September 1807, The North River Steam Boat advertisement, New York State Library BOX 409
evidence.supports: The printed advertisement offers an Albany passage from Paulas Hook ferry on Friday, 4 September, and lists a fare of seven dollars for Albany.

evidence.locator: pp. 104–105, extracts dated September and October 1807
evidence.supports: The guide reproduces a September 1807 advertisement for the North River steamboat listing a seven-dollar Paule’s Hook–Albany fare, and an October 2 report of a departure with ninety passengers; these are reported offer and passenger counts.

events.caveats: The seven dollars was an advertised fare. The notice gives the planned itinerary. A separately documented passenger account records the actual passage.

date.label: 4–5 September 1807
date.basis: The passenger statement describes Friday departure and is dated at Albany on 5 September. Wilson’s account identifies the Friday as 4 September.

events.statement: The North River Steamboat carried passengers from New York to Albany on its first packet passage. Passengers signed an account of the completed voyage.
events.scope: First advertised packet passage from New York to Albany

evidence.locator: Vol. VI, pp. 23 and 25, Wilson’s account and passenger statement dated 5 September 1807
evidence.supports: Passenger John Q. Wilson places the opening packet on Friday, 4 September. His account reprints the signed passenger statement, dated at Albany on 5 September, which records a Friday departure from New York and arrival at Albany.

events.caveats: The 1807 statement survives here in an 1855 reprint. The account documents travel and arrival. It gives no fare collected from a named passenger.

date.label: 15 September 1810
date.basis: Date of Fulton’s letter to Boulton & Watt.

events.statement: In a letter to Boulton & Watt, Robert Fulton identified their 1804 engine as powering his New York–Albany passenger boat. He described it by its 24-inch cylinder and four-foot stroke.
events.scope: Fulton’s retrospective identification of the engine used in the Hudson passenger service

evidence.locator: pp. 230–231, Fulton to Boulton & Watt, 15 September 1810 (MS 3147/3/496, item 15)
evidence.supports: Fulton identifies the engine made for him in 1804, with a 24-inch cylinder and four-foot stroke, as powering a boat carrying passengers between New York and Albany. He separately orders another engine.

evidence.locator: pp. 177–178, Boulton & Watt account of 17 January and letter of 21 February 1805
evidence.supports: The account names Robert Fulton and specifies engine materials for a 24-inch cylinder and four-foot stroke. Boulton & Watt’s letter says the goods were forwarded for delivery to his London address.

events.caveats: The date is that of the letter. The manufacturer’s engine code and the transatlantic freight entry remain unverified.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest event for this scoped capability established by the inspected passages; no global priority is inferred.

research.note: The passenger account, newspaper facsimile and engine correspondence are proposed additions for independent review.

unresolved.about: Manufacturer’s engine code and overseas delivery
unresolved.note: The maker’s account and Fulton’s service letter match by customer, engine dimensions and order history. The order-book folio, engine code, transatlantic shipping record and installation handover remain unverified. The records support supply to the Hudson service. Any identity with another named Soho installation in the catalogue remains unverified.
